short: A British first-rate ship of the line, most famous as Lord Nelson's flagship at Trafalgar.
full:
Launched in 1765, HMS Victory is a massive 104-gun first-rate ship of the line. She was placed in reserve for thirteen years before seeing active service during the American War of Independence and the French Revolutionary Wars. She gained lasting fame as Vice-Admiral Horatio Nelson's flagship during the Battle of Trafalgar in 1805.

At Trafalgar, Victory broke the French and Spanish line, securing a decisive British triumph, though Nelson was fatally wounded on her quarterdeck. She was retired from active combat in 1812 but remained in various auxiliary roles. Today, she is preserved in Portsmouth as a museum ship and holds the distinction of being the world's oldest naval vessel still in commission.
